name: The k-th derivative Fourier identity ĉₙ(f⁽ᵏ⁾) = (i·n)ᵏ·ĉₙ(f)

insights: Isoperimetric (Hurwitz Fourier) lineage. Grandparent oq-02-oq-02 proves the first-order IBP identity ĉₙ(f') = i·n·ĉₙ(f); parent oq-02-oq-02-oq-02 iterates once for ĉₙ(f'') = −n²·ĉₙ(f). This child CLOSES THE INDUCTION: ĉₙ(f⁽ᵏ⁾) = (i·n)ᵏ·ĉₙ(f) for smooth periodic f and every k.
This is the spectral statement behind the whole Fourier approach: differentiation acts diagonally on the Fourier basis with eigenvalue i·n, so d^{2m} has eigenvalue (i·n)^{2m} = (−1)^m·n^{2m}.

Proof = clean induction on k. Step rewrites f⁽ᵏ⁺¹⁾ = (f')⁽ᵏ⁾ via Function.iterate_succ_apply, applies the IH to the smooth periodic function f' (universally quantifying f INSIDE the ∀ so the IH is available at deriv f), then peels one factor i·n with the grandparent first-order identity. Smoothness preserved by contDiff_infty_iff_deriv; periodicity preserved by parent's deriv_periodic_of_periodic.

Smoothness uses ContDiff ℝ ∞ (C^∞), dodging the finite-C^k succ/cast bookkeeping. KEY API in Lean v4.26 Mathlib: ContDiff smoothness lives in WithTop ℕ∞ where ∞ = ((⊤:ℕ∞):WithTop ℕ∞) is NOT the order-top ⊤ (=ω, analytic). So `1 ≤ ∞` is NOT le_top; use `hf.of_le (by exact_mod_cast le_top)` (mathlib's own idiom). ∞ notation is `open scoped ContDiff`. ContDiff.iterate_deriv / contDiff_infty_iff_deriv / contDiff_infty (↔ ∀n:ℕ, ContDiff n) are the smooth-deriv toolkit.

Corollaries: fourierCoeffOn_deriv2_smooth recovers the parent's −n² as k=2 ((I·n)²=−n² via Complex.I_sq); fourierCoeffOn_iteratedDeriv_even gives the d^{2m} eigenvalue (−1)^m·n^{2m} (mul_pow+pow_mul+I_sq).
